'''Shelly Monica Jones''' (born November 2, 1964) is an American [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]]. She is an associate professor of mathematics education at [[Central Connecticut State University]].

==Early life and education==
Jones is African-American; she was raised in [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]] and went on to study computer science at [[Spelman College]], graduating in 1986.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=25 February 2019|title=Black History Month Honoree 2019: Shelly M. Jones|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/shelly-m-jones/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=4 June 2020|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Alumnae Features : Dr. Shelly Jones|url=https://www.spelmanwomentowatch.com/drsmjones-c86|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=4 June 2020|website=Spelman Women to Watch}}</ref> Jones received a master's degree in [[mathematics education]] from the [[University of Bridgeport]] and a Ph.D. in mathematics education from [[Illinois State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Provost|first=Kerri|date=|title=Women in Science Spotlight: Dr. Shelly M. Jones|url=https://ctsciencecenter.org/blog/women-in-science-spotlight-dr-shelly-m-jones/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=4 June 2020|website=Connecticut Space Center}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Jones is an associate professor at [[Central Connecticut State University]] in New Britain, Connecticut.  She teaches undergraduate and graduate content, curriculum, and methods courses.  Her focus includes culturally relevant mathematics, where she explains cognitively demanding mathematics skills from a relevant cultural perspective.<ref name=":0" /> In addition, Jones's specialties include integrating elementary school mathematics and music, and the effects of college students’ attitudes and beliefs about mathematics on their success in college.  

Jones' accomplishments have earned her recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2019 Honoree.<ref name=":0" />

==Book==
Jones is the author of the book ''Women Who Count: Honoring African American Women Mathematicians'', published in 2019 by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>''Women Who Count: Honoring African American Women Mathematicians'', {{ISBN|978-1470448899}}. Reviews:
* {{cite journal|title=none|journal=[[Mathematical Reviews]]|first=Amanda|last=Knecht|mr=3966443}}
* {{cite web|title=Women Who Count|work=MAA Reviews|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|first=Geoffrey|last=Dietz|date=November 2019|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/women-who-count}}
* {{cite journal|last=Clark|first=Kathleen M.|date=June 2020|doi=10.1080/26375451.2020.1778282|journal=British Journal for the History of Mathematics|pages=253–255|title=none|volume=35|issue=3|s2cid=222003448|doi-access=free}}</ref>
